bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets

facts.statement: A tentative trendline is drawn by connecting two initial reaction lows in an uptrend or two rally highs in a downtrend. It only becomes a valid, authoritative trendline after a third test where prices touch the line and successfully bounce off it in the direction of the prevailing trend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Tentative Trendline: A straight line drawn connecting two initial reaction lows... Valid Trendline: confirmed by a third test [4-6].

facts.statement: Because any straight line requires at least two points to establish a trajectory, a tentative trendline is geometrically projected across time using two initial reaction low or rally peak coordinates, where confirmation occurs when a third price point satisfies the projected line equation and reverses.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: If P1(t1) and P2(t2) are two reaction lows at times t1 and t2, the tentative trendline equation is P(t) = P1 + ((P2 - P1)/(t2 - t1))(t - t1) [4-6].

variables.definition: Projected trendline price at time t
Price at the first reaction low or rally high
Price at the second reaction low or rally high
Time coordinate of the first anchor point
Time coordinate of the second anchor point
Current or target time coordinate being evaluated

facts.statement: Correct trendline construction requires drawing the line directly under the entire day's price range in an uptrend or over the entire day's range in a downtrend, encompassing all intraday high and low shadow extremes rather than connecting only daily closing prices.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Trendlines must be drawn over or under the entire day's price range (including high and low shadow extremes), not just closing prices [7].

facts.statement: When price temporarily violates an up trendline intraday but recovers to close back above it, analysts should avoid immediately discarding the line; instead, they retain the original solid trendline while drawing a secondary dotted line under the new intraday low until subsequent market action reveals which slope is truer.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: If price dips beneath an up trendline intraday but closes back above it, a compromise technique is to retain the original trendline while drawing a secondary dotted trendline [8, 9].

facts.statement: The analytical weight and structural authority of a valid trendline are governed by two distinct metrics: the duration it has remained intact without violation (such as nine months versus nine days) and the total number of successful price tests it has withstood (such as eight touches versus three).

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: The significance of a trendline increases with length of time intact (e.g., 9 months vs. 9 days) and number of times tested (e.g., 8 successful tests vs. 3) [10].

facts.statement: In an established uptrend, pullbacks toward the up trendline serve as low-risk buying zones, whereas rallies to a down trendline in a downtrend offer selling zones; however, a decisive closing violation of a valid trendline signals a trend reversal and mandates liquidating all positions aligned with the prior trend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Dips toward the up trendline are primary buying areas... A decisive closing break of a valid trendline signals a trend change and mandates liquidating positions [3, 11].

facts.statement: On the weekly bar chart of the KBW Bank Index, a long-term tentative up trendline was anchored along two major reaction lows formed across 1995 and 1996. At the beginning of 1998, a third corrective reaction low touched and rebounded directly off this line, confirming its validity and preserving the primary uptrend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: KBW Bank Index (Weekly Bar Chart): long-term up trendline drawn along two 1995–1996 reaction lows. A third reaction low at the start of 1998 bounced directly off this trendline [12].

facts.statement: To eliminate false intraday penetrations and whipsaws on major trendlines or support levels, the 3% price filter requires the market to break and close beyond the trendline by at least 3% of the price level at the point of penetration, though this rule is excluded from interest rate futures.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Requires price to break and close beyond a major trendline by at least 3%... P_trigger = P_line * (1 - 0.03) [13, 14].

variables.definition: Required closing price threshold to confirm a valid downside breakout
Exact price value of the trendline at the point of penetration

facts.statement: While long-term analysis relies on a 3% price filter, shorter-term swing traders scale down to a 1% filter or a 1 full point threshold in equities. Traders face an inherent tradeoff: an overly small filter fails to prevent costly whipsaws, whereas an overly large filter forfeits a substantial portion of the initial move.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Shorter-term trading uses a 1% filter; stock chartists may require a 1 full point move... If a filter is too small, it fails to eliminate whipsaws; if too large, a significant portion of the initial price move is missed [14].

facts.statement: As an alternative to percentage price thresholds, time filters validate breakouts through duration: the 2-day rule requires prices to close beyond the violated trendline, neckline, or support level for two consecutive trading sessions, while weekly chart analysis mandates a decisive Friday closing price beyond the breakout boundary.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: 2-Day Time Filter: Requires prices to close beyond the trendline for two consecutive trading days... Friday Close Filter: Requires a Friday close beyond the breakout point [15-17].

facts.statement: When evaluating a major up trendline in the gold market positioned at $400 per ounce, applying the 3% price filter requires a downside penetration of at least $12 ($400 multiplied by 0.03), meaning gold must record a daily closing price at or below $388 to confirm a valid sell signal.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Gold Market Numerical Example: major up trendline in gold broken at $400... gold must close $12 below the line (400 * 0.03 = 12), requiring a closing price at or below $388 [14].

facts.statement: Once a valid trendline experiences a decisive, filter-confirmed penetration, its structural role permanently reverses: a broken up trendline transitions from a dynamic support floor into an overhead resistance ceiling on subsequent recovery rallies, while a broken down trendline converts from overhead resistance into a support floor on subsequent pullbacks.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: When a support or resistance level (or trendline) is broken by a significant margin, it reverses its structural role and becomes its opposite [18-22].

facts.statement: Role reversal is driven by trader regret among longs, shorts, and uncommitted participants: buyers who entered at prior trendline support become trapped in losing positions when the line breaks, causing them to aggressively liquidate at break-even during subsequent return bounces, which transforms former buying demand into overhead selling supply.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Longs who bought at support suffer losses when price drops; on subsequent bounces back to that price level, they rush to liquidate at break-even, transforming prior buying interest into heavy sell orders [23, 24].

facts.statement: Because role reversal takes effect following a confirmed breakout, chartists must extend all violated trendlines far to the right on their charts; these extended lines capture return moves where prices rally to fail at the underside of broken up trendlines or dip to hold the top side of broken down trendlines.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.excerpt: Line Extension: Always extend all broken trendlines far out to the right on charts, as they frequently serve as major support/resistance barriers in the future [20-22].

generalAssumptions: Market action discounts all known and unknown fundamentals.
Prices move in trends, and a trend in motion is more likely to continue than to reverse.
History repeats itself as recurring chart patterns reflect consistent human market psychology.
